public.title: Continuous Line XII (silence)
public.material: 6 in. ID corrugated HDPE pipe, part stainless steel hardware
public.text: A site-specific sculpture made with student collaborator Nick Allario ’29 and the first to use LineWorks, a custom tool that generates linear geometry from sound recordings. The form is a physical manifestation of Silence, a speech by Prof. Joel Relihan delivered at Wheaton’s Honors Convocation in May 2026. Suspended overhead in the atrium of Knapton Hall.

public.title: Continuous Line XI (yellow)
public.material: 9 & 7 inch dia. HDPE corrugated pipe, paint
public.size: 240 ft of material, installation dimensions variable
public.text: Made with student collaborator Nick Allario ’29 from recyclable industrial drain pipe, which is pliable enough to be shaped intuitively while responding to the architecture and landscape of the site. The color ties the form to Wheaton’s institutional branding as well as to its geometry. One playful “trajectory” among countless others across a campus of pathfinding and trailblazing.

studio.title: Crates
studio.material: Alaskan timber, harvested and processed by hand at its origin and then shipped east in the form of crates
studio.size: Two largest crates, 24 × 24 × 72 in.; installation, 2 × 6 × 14 ft
studio.text: The crates traveled by boat, planes, and trucks and inherit the marks of transit each time they are exhibited. The two largest crates, which hold the remaining 12 crates, are the maximum dimensions shippable via standard UPS. The installation of empty crates contains a separate, embedded musical work, Passage, 2014, which plays on headphones. Passage was created in collaboration with the composer Ben Wasserman (5 min 39 sec).

studio.title: Two Views
studio.material: Two-channel video installation, 10 min. loop. For back-to-back televisions or dual projection
studio.text: Created by facing two cameras at each other with 1920 km between them, bridging the shortest distance between the artist’s country of birth and country of residence. Left camera: southernmost point of the USA, Key West, FL (24.545570, -81.783306), heading 137.4° SE, downward pitch 8.8°. Right camera: northernmost point of Curaçao, Watamula (12.390646, -69.156179), heading 317.4° NW, downward pitch 8.8°. Exhibited as back-to-back projections. Continuous loop. Silent.
